Basin-hop the jammed record by re-inserting rattlers into largest voids and shaking overloaded hubs, then anneal a LogSumExp max-cosine with Adam on the sphere before final LP polish.

Basin-hopping with softmax max-cosine smoothing and targeted re-initialization of jammed points plus short trust-region LP squeezes to jump basins.
Basin-hopping around the record with rattler teleportation, hub-targeted shakes and fast exponential soft-max repulsion smoothing followed by short trust-region LP refinements.
Basin-hopping from the record with targeted shakes of overloaded points and void-reinsertion of the worst point followed by short trust-region LP polishes and a final long polish.
Basin-hopping with rattler reinsertion and overload-targeted kicks followed by annealed soft-max repulsion (Adam) and trust-region LP polishing to change contact topology.

Hybrid basin-hopping that escapes the isolated 2-pair maximum with contact-guided kicks (hub shake, worst-subset reinit, rattler-to-void reinsertion) alternating LogSumExp Adam annealing and top-K max-pair descent, plus widened trust-region LP squeezes.
Iterate small Gaussian basin kicks with annealed soft-max Adam on the sphere and trust-region LP equalization of the whole near-max cluster to lower the minimax cosine.

Stress-guided basin hopping that relieves overloaded hubs and fills voids via targeted reinsertion plus cap rotations, each kick followed by sharpening LogSumExp Adam annealing on the sphere and trust-region tangent LP snapping.
Alternate coherent basin-changing moves with fast LogSumExp Adam annealing on the sphere to change contact topology and exact trust-region LP polish only for promising basins.
Elitist basin-hopping with worst-point void reinsertion and patch shattering plus LogSumExp Adam annealing on the sphere, followed by trust-region LP and greedy pair micro-polish.
Basin-hopping with jammed-cluster expansion, rattler-to-void reinsertion and top-balanced LogSumExp annealing plus adaptive trust-region LP squeezes to jump basins.

Break the isolated worst pair with targeted pair-splitting, coherent cap rotations and void reinsertion, each followed by annealed soft-max Adam and widened trust-region LP to change contact topology.

Coordinate-wise greedy basin moves that directly attack the isolated worst pair by re-optimizing one endpoint at a time with batched tangent sampling, alternating with soft-max Adam and trust-region LP equalization.
Elitist tiny-kick search that squeezes the isolated maximal pair with top-K exact line-search descent plus tight top-P trust-region LP and high-K softmax Adam.

Basin-hopping with void reinsertion, jammed-cluster expansion and antipodal symmetrization alternating sharp LogSumExp Adam, top-K minimax descent and wide-margin trust-region LP equalization of the whole near-max plateau.

Alternate broad LogSumExp Adam annealing to lower the bulk of near-contacts with sharp bottleneck-only descent and narrow-window trust-region LP to squeeze the isolated 2-pair maximum, driven by contact-guided kicks that force topology changes.

Break the isolated max pair with contact-guided void reinsertion and two-scale descent (broad LogSumExp Adam plus tight top-K max descent) alternated with small-window trust-region LP equalization of the ~1300-pair plateau.
Attack the isolated worst pair with alternating pair-splitting and coordinate-wise void sampling, interleaved with annealed soft-max Adam and trust-region LP to change contact topology.

Split the isolated worst pair and rotate coherent caps to change contact topology, reinsert overloaded points into voids, then anneal with balanced soft-max Adam, widened trust-region LP, and greedy single-point micro hill-climbing.

Elitist basin-hopping that alternates annealed soft-max Adam with vectorized single-point minimax coordinate descent and sparse trust-region LP, using worst-pair splits, coherent cap shifts and large-sample void reinsertion to change contact topology.

Directly attack the isolated worst pair with coordinate-wise void search and single-point softmax refinement, fused with pair-splitting and cap-rotation kicks followed by annealed softmax Adam and trust-region LP.
Attack the isolated worst pair with symmetric pair-splitting and joint resampling plus void reinsertion, alternating with annealed soft-max Adam and trust-region LP to reshape the flat plateau.
Void-targeted basin hopping that alternates LogSumExp Adam annealing with exact single-point void re-optimization of the isolated worst pair plus trust-region LP equalization.
Bulk hub surgery deleting 8-48 high-participation points and greedily reinserting from 200k candidates with frozen-set Adam refinement then joint LSE+LP repolish.
direction: Use bulk delete-and-reinsert surgery targeted at the near-contact network: compute each point's participation count in the top 1,500 pairs and its row maximum, delete k points in separate trials for k in {8, 16, 32, 48} (half highest-participation hubs, half sampled from the remaining high-row-max points), freeze the survivors, generate at least 200,000 spherical candidates, and greedily insert replacements one at a time by minimizing each candidate's maximum cosine to the frozen plus already-inserted points, locally refining each inserted point on the sphere against that frozen set for 50-100 Adam steps before inserting the next. After all replacements, unfreeze everything and repolish with LogSumExp Adam followed by plateau-wide LP, retaining the surgery only if the top-1, top-100, and top-1,000 cosines improve, thereby changing contact topology at a scale inaccessible to single-point kicks.

idea: De novo multi-basin census with annealed Riesz energies plus Procrustes-Hungarian crossover of low-row-max halves and void refill.
direction: Run a genuinely de novo multi-basin census and crossover experiment that does not start from best.npy: initialize at least 12 independent random codes, minimize Riesz-type energies sum_{i<j} ((1+<x_i,x_j>)/2)^{p/2} with p annealed through 8, 32, 128, and 512 (about 300 Adam steps per stage), then apply sharp LogSumExp minimization and LP polishing to each, and archive the distinct minima classified by their sorted Gram spectra and near-contact counts. For the best few genetically different parents, align them by orthogonal Procrustes after Hungarian matching on pairwise cosine distance (scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment), construct children from the 128 lowest-row-max points of each parent, remove near-duplicates and refill from spherical voids, and repolish; this tests whether the record basin itself is the limitation and provides structurally new incumbents for Directions 1 and 3.

idea: Escape the single-contact basin with symmetry-supported balanced starts (full and partial sign-flip orbits plus Riesz-spread random restarts) then elitist basin-hopping with void reinsertion, cap rotations and balanced Riesz plus soft-max Adam before greedy minimax and LP polishing.
Seed jammed basins with sign-group symmetric codes then break symmetry and mix them into the incumbent via rotation-aligned block transplants and quantile-equalized hopping.

Diverse-basin hopping that combines global void re-insertion, coherent-cap rotations and subset shakes with soft-max Adam annealing and wide-window trust-region LP equalization to escape the single-contact plateau toward a highly-contacted basin.
Search symmetry-generated codes with balanced contact networks under 64-element sign-flip plus pair-swap groups, then release symmetry for unconstrained refinement.
direction: Search symmetry-generated codes that automatically possess balanced contact networks: fix a 64-element subgroup of O(6), for example all 32 even-parity diagonal sign flips combined with swapping the coordinate pairs (1,2)(3,4)(5,6), parametrize only four generic seed vectors, expand each under the group to obtain exactly 256 points, and optimize the resulting 24 seed coordinates with annealed LogSumExp Adam (K from 100 to 3000). Try many random seed initializations and at least one alternative group, such as sign flips combined with cyclic permutation of the three coordinate pairs, select the best symmetric code, then gradually release the symmetry by running unconstrained Adam and the wide-active-set LP from Direction 1; this can discover a qualitatively different, rigid basin rather than another perturbation of the record.

idea: Start from unions of four randomly rotated ±1 cubes (already 0.667 intra-cube and highly contacted) then spread with Riesz energy and anneal with LogSumExp Adam to reach a balanced basin before sharp minimax and LP polish.

Active-set tangent LP equalizer that linearizes all near-max pairs and alternates max-t and sum-load LPs under cycling trust radii.
direction: Build a true active-set equalizer rather than another softmax polish: from `best.npy`, take all pairs with slack below $3\times10^{-4}$ (about 1400 pairs), parametrize each displacement in a local 5D tangent basis (1280 variables plus $t$), and repeatedly solve with HiGHS the LP minimizing $t$ subject to linearized pair cosines $\le t$, with trust radii cycling $3\times10^{-4},10^{-4},3\times10^{-5},10^{-5}$ and exact renormalization after each step. Add a lexicographic second LP at fixed near-optimal $t$ minimizing the sum of the top 1500 linearized cosines to spread load, accept a step if the true maximum decreases or if the number of pairs tied within $10^{-8}$ increases without increasing the maximum, and reserve the last 20 seconds to return the best iterate; this directly seeks the missing exactly tied, multi-contact-per-point graph.

Build 256 points as four 64-element sign-flip orbits from |x|-clustered prototypes with |coord|>=0.12, optimize prototypes with high-K softmax and prototype LP, then release symmetry in staged noisy Adam+LP.
direction: Search for a symmetry-balanced construction from scratch, using four generic orbits of the 64-element sign-flip group ($4\times64=256$) but initializing the four prototypes from clusters of $|x_i|$ in the incumbent rather than randomly, enforcing all prototype coordinates to have magnitude at least 0.12 to avoid orbit collapse, and optimizing only the 24 prototype coordinates with high-$K$ softmax ($K:200\to20000$) followed by prototype-space LP so symmetry forces equal contact counts within each orbit. Then break symmetry in stages with tangent noise of amplitudes $0,10^{-4},10^{-3},10^{-2}$, fully releasing all 256 points for Adam and LP after each stage and retaining the best stage; this is a deliberate attempt to inherit balanced contacts from symmetry before asymmetry is allowed.

idea: Cardinality homotopy through N=240,248,264,272 with void insertion and leave-one-out deletion to escape the single-pair plateau, then rejamming back to 256.
direction: Use cardinality homotopy to change contact topology: construct codes with $N=240,248,264,$ and $272$ by deleting points with the smallest row-maximum from the incumbent or greedily inserting void points chosen from at least 200k random candidates, optimize each size with annealed softmax Adam and the Direction-1 LP, then convert back to 256 by inserting points four at a time into the currently largest spherical voids (rejamming after each insertion) or, for $N>256$, deleting the point whose leave-one-out removal most lowers the resulting maximum. Keep any intermediate whose projected 256-point score beats the incumbent, because adding/removing points destroys the present single-pair plateau instead of perturbing inside it.

idea: Diverse pool with Procrustes-Hungarian mating of coherent blocks and void refill plus archive by Gram distance.
direction: Maintain a diverse pool and mate distinct basins instead of repeatedly perturbing one incumbent: generate 10–12 shallow-polished optima using tangent-noise scales 0.03, 0.08, and 0.15 plus independent random restarts, align each pair of diverse optima by orthogonal Procrustes followed by Hungarian assignment on cosine similarity, and create children by transplanting PCA- or contact-community-coherent blocks of 32, 64, or 128 points, deleting any transplanted point closer than the current threshold to a retained point and greedily refilling from void candidates. Score children by maximum cosine but maintain the archive using both score and Gram-matrix distance so near-duplicates are discarded, spend about 130 seconds on generation and mating, then apply a deep LP polish only to the best two children and always fall back to the loaded incumbent if none improves.

idea: Escape the single-contact plateau with large basin-hopping perturbations and moderate-K LogSumExp Adam that equally weights the ~1400 near-tied pairs to equalize contacts, plus top-k uniform-force refinement and final tangent-LP polishing.
Escape the single-pair plateau with diverse de novo basins plus void-refill and hub-kick hopping optimized under moderate-K softmax that pulls the whole near-contact plateau down together.

Bottleneck-cluster surgery that deletes the top neighbourhood around the max pair and greedily reinserts from a large random pool with single-point LSE refinement plus cluster-joint Adam and LP polish.
direction: Targeted bottleneck-cluster surgery: Identify the attaining pair $(i,j)$ and take its near-contact neighbourhood — all points with cosine $>0.60$ to $i$ or $j$, expected to be a few dozen points — delete that cluster (try sizes 12, 20, 32), and freeze the remaining $\sim$224 points. Reinsert the deleted points one at a time from a pool of 200,000 random sphere points plus tangent perturbations of the deleted originals, choosing each candidate to minimise its maximum cosine to the frozen-plus-already-reinserted set, then refine each inserted point against that frozen set with 75 steps of single-point LSE-Adam ($K=2500$, lr $0.02$). Follow with a cluster-only joint Adam phase, then a full LP polish, and repeat over at least 20 seeds; retain a result only if it reduces both $c_0$ and the number of pairs within $10^{-4}$ of $c_0$. This attacks exactly the points responsible for the wall around the bottleneck instead of perturbing rattlers at random.

idea: Four rotated hypercubes with Cayley-parametrised relative rotations optimised by Adam on cross-copy LSE then symmetry release and polish.
direction: Symmetry-structured construction from four rotated hypercubes: Build a de novo, rattler-free ansatz as four rotated copies of the 64 vertices of $\{\pm1\}^6/\sqrt6$ (within-copy maximum cosine is fixed at $2/3$, safely below target), giving exactly 256 points. Parameterise the three relative rotations by skew-symmetric $6\times6$ matrices via the Cayley transform (45 free parameters, first copy fixed as identity) and optimise only these parameters with Adam on a log-sum-exp of all cross-copy cosines ($K$ annealed $200\to5000$), which by construction keeps every point equivalent within its copy and produces a dense, balanced contact pattern. Try 8–12 random rotation initialisations within the time budget, take the best, then release the symmetry — perturb by $10^{-3}$ in random tangent directions, run full LSE-Adam and LP polish — and return whichever of this released code or the loaded incumbent scores lower.

idea: Joint plateau lowering with worst-point void ejection and greedy farthest-point reinsertion to force a spanning balanced contact network instead of polishing the single bottleneck pair.

idea: Plateau-first lexicographic search alternating CVaR Adam and wide-margin tangent LP with strict spectrum acceptance
direction: Plateau-first lexicographic optimisation: Starting from `best.npy`, do not minimise only $c_0$ (the maximum cosine); compute the sorted cosine spectrum and lexicographically minimise $(c_0, c_{100}, c_{1000}, \mathrm{mean\ of\ top\ 1500})$ with $c_0$ allowed to rise temporarily by up to $5\times10^{-5}$. Alternate (a) Adam on a CVaR objective — mean of the top 200 cosines plus $0.3\times$ mean of cosines ranked 201–1500 plus a log-sum-exp max term, with $K$ annealed $500\to8000$ — and (b) the tangent LP with its active-set margin deliberately widened to $10^{-4}$ (up to $\sim$2500 pairs, cycling trust radii $10^{-3},3\times10^{-4},10^{-4},3\times10^{-5}$). Accept a step only if the sorted spectrum improves lexicographically (compare $c_{100}$ before celebrating a $c_0$ gain), run 6–10 such cycles, and always fall back to the loaded incumbent if nothing beats it; success means the $2\times10^{-8}$ plateau is pushed down as a whole, after which a strict LP polish converts it into a genuinely lower $c_0$.

Delete k high-contact plus random points, hard-anneal survivors with Riesz plus LP to a lower-density basin, then greedy void-refill regrowth with batch refits.
direction: Delete-to-lower-density continuation and greedy regrowth: Exploit that codes with fewer points can reach a much lower maximum: delete $k\in\{16,32,48\}$ points (half chosen for highest participation in pairs above $0.68$, half at random), optimise the remaining $256-k$ points hard with Riesz annealing ($p$ from 20 to 200) plus LP until their maximum is at least $3\times10^{-3}$ below the incumbent, then regrow one point at a time — each new point chosen from 200,000 candidates to minimise its maximum cosine to the current set, refined by single-point Adam, with a joint LSE+LP refit after every batch of 8 insertions and backtracking (re-optimise all points, retry a different void) whenever an insertion pushes the maximum above $0.7055$. Cycle this drill-and-refill process with different deletion sets, scoring candidates on $(c_0,c_{100})$ rather than $c_0$ alone, and keep the global incumbent as a guaranteed fallback output.
